predecessors.name: Satavahana dynasty
predecessors.text: the Chutu core where Cliopatria draws the Satavahana shape (102 of 228 cells, 106-223)

successors.name: Kadamba dynasty
successors.text: Banavasi in Uttara Kannada and its country: "northern Karnataka" (the Satavahana page's south-western kingdom of the Chutus of Banavasi)

ledger.x: c. 125: Chutu rule begins at Banavasi. The page: "c. 125 CE: Chutu rule at Banavasi begins" (Michael Mitchiner speculates they were Shaka chiefs who became Satavahana feudatories after Gautamiputra Satakarni defeated Nahapana around 125 CE); infobox "1st century BCE" as established and "3rd century CE" as…

c. 345: the Kadambas occupy Banavasi. "c. 345 CE: The Kadambas occupy Banavasi, which ends Chutu rule there." The page also says the line "came to an end probably in the first or second half of the third century, that is, around 250-275 CE", which contradicts its own c. 345.

c. 345: Chutu rule ends at Banavasi under the Kadambas. Four Chutu inscriptions are dated within the 260s-340s, and an Abhira inscription from Nagarjunakonda of 278 attests King Sivalananda, which supports a life beyond 275.

wars.name: Kadamba occupation of Banavasi
wars.outcome: The Kadambas occupy Banavasi and end Chutu rule there.

certainty.note: No border is given for any year; the extent is Banavasi and its country, with coin finds at Anantapur and southern Telangana and subordinate places in Goa not drawn.
